title: Lupita Nyong’o Joins Nairobi City Thunder Ownership Group
desc: Lupita Nyong’o has invested in Nairobi City Thunder as the Kenyan club prepares for the 2026 KNBL Finals against Kenya Ports Authority.
content:
Oscar-winning Kenyan actress Lupita Nyong’o has joined the ownership group of Nairobi City Thunder, adding her name to the basketball club’s growing list of high-profile backers ahead of the 2026 Kenya National Basketball League (KNBL) Finals.

Nyong’o announced the investment on Thursday, September 24, saying she was proud to support the Nairobi-based club and its progress in African basketball. Her announcement has continued to draw attention in Kenyan sports coverage on Friday.

The actress highlighted Thunder’s achievement of becoming the first Kenyan team to qualify for the Basketball Africa League (BAL), describing herself as proud to be behind the club.

Her entry into the ownership group comes at an important point in Thunder’s domestic campaign. The team is preparing to face Kenya Ports Authority (KPA) in the 2026 KNBL Finals, with the best-of-five series scheduled to begin on Saturday, September 26, in Mombasa.

According to KBC, the opening two games will be played at Makande Gymnasium on September 26 and 27 before the series moves to Nairobi for Game Three on October 2 at Nyayo Gymnasium.

Thunder reached the final after sweeping Stanbic Shields 3-0 in the semifinals. KPA also secured its place in the championship series after completing a 3-0 semifinal sweep against Equity Dumas.

The club has also built a significant continental profile. FIBA records Nairobi City Thunder as the 2026 East Division Elite 16 champions, while the team secured its place in the 2026 BAL after winning its Road to BAL campaign.

Thunder’s BAL journey has given the club a wider platform beyond the Kenyan league. Its qualification for the continental competition marked a milestone for Kenyan basketball and has helped attract greater attention to the local game.

Nyong’o’s investment now comes alongside the club’s preparations for another domestic title campaign. Her involvement also follows recent investment activity around the team, with musician Bien-Aimé Baraza and Chiki Kuruka also joining the ownership structure, according to Pulse Kenya.

For Kenyan basketball supporters, the immediate focus now shifts to the KNBL Finals, where Thunder will begin its title defence against KPA.

The investment itself was announced on September 24, while Friday’s coverage places the development in the context of the weekend’s championship series and Thunder’s expanding presence in Kenyan and African basketball.
